official.deadline_note: Applications are accepted throughout the year; each evaluation round has a hard cutoff. From the Autumn 2027 selection round, that is for all applications submitted after 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET, re-applications will no longer be permitted.
official.application_cycle: Rolling applications with evaluation rounds; next hard cutoff 22 January 2027
official.status_note: The EMBO fellowship page states that applications are accepted throughout the year, with the next cutoff date - a hard deadline - on Friday 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET.
benefits: EMBO provides grants for host institutions in EMBC Member States to issue employment contracts to EMBO Fellows; fellows working in other countries receive a stipend.
Salary or stipend for the postdoctoral position, at a rate that depends on the country being visited.
Travel and relocation allowance paid as a lump sum, ideally before the start date of the fellowship.
Child daycare allowance up to EUR 2,500 per fellowship year and per child for children under six (non-EMBC fellows only).
Dependent child allowance for children under 18 (non-EMBC fellows only); the value depends on the country visited.
Free attendance at an EMBO Laboratory Leadership Course, and membership of the EMBO Fellows' Network.
eligibility: Applicants must hold a doctorate or equivalent at the start of the fellowship.
Applicants who already hold a PhD at the time of application are eligible only if they obtained it during the two years prior to the date the application is submitted.

Applicants must have at least one first author publication accepted in or published in an international peer reviewed journal at the time of application, or a first author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews from an independent peer review service.
All applications must involve movement between countries; applications to go to the country in which the PhD was obtained will not be considered.

Applications will not be considered to return to a laboratory where the candidate worked for more than six months in total, or to the laboratory, institute or department where the PhD was obtained or with the former PhD supervisor.

The project must not be a direct continuation of the PhD work, and candidates who have already started working in the host laboratory may apply only if they have been living in the host country for less than six months at the time of application.
requirements: One application for one project at one host laboratory at each round of selection.
Doctoral supervisor's support and a host laboratory in a host institution.
Agreement with the host institution that the EMBO grant is used to fund an employment contract for the fellow.
Fellowships must be started within one calendar year from the relevant evaluation cut-off.
documents: Online application via the EMBO application portal.
Confirmation of the host supervisor and host institution.
First-author publication or verifiably peer-reviewed first-author preprint.
selection_criteria: The international mobility of the project.
coverage: A salary or stipend for the postdoctoral position at a country-dependent rate, intended to cover the cost of living in the host country.
Travel and relocation allowance as a lump sum.

Published rates for 2026, applicable to fellowships awarded in Autumn 2025 and onwards: EUR 51,600 to 99,600 per fellowship year for EMBC Member States (for example 89,400 Germany, 86,400 Belgium, 75,600 France, 97,200 Switzerland, 75,000 Italy and UK), and 28,200 to 65,400 for non-EMBC countries (for example 65,400 US, 63,600 Singapore, 51,000 Australia and Taiwan, 46,800 Canada, 39,600 India, 28,200 Chile).
EMBO explicitly does not cover bench fees, overheads, funds for consumables or any other financial benefits to the host supervisor or receiving institute.
application_method: Apply online through the EMBO application portal at http://applications.embo.org/01/register.php?reg=S019.
Submit before the hard cutoff of the relevant evaluation round - the next is Friday 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET.
Fellowships must be started within one calendar year of the relevant evaluation cut-off.
official.application_route: One online application per selection round through the EMBO application portal, submitted before the round's hard cutoff.
official.study_mode: Full-time or part-time at 50% or 75% may be requested; the maximum combined full-time and part-time duration must not exceed 36 months.
official.international_eligibility: Open to postdoctoral researchers of any nationality; international mobility is a key requirement and all applications must involve movement between countries.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Life sciences; the fellowship supports excellent postdoctoral researchers in the life sciences throughout Europe and the world.
official.research_requirement: A postdoctoral research project that is not a direct continuation of the PhD work, hosted in a laboratory where the candidate has not previously worked.
official.duration: Awarded for a period of two years although shorter durations can be requested; the minimum is one year, and the maximum combined full-time and part-time duration must not exceed 36 months.
official.description: EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships support excellent postdoctoral researchers throughout Europe and the world for a period of up to two years. International mobility is a key requirement, and the fellowship includes a salary or stipend, a relocation allowance and support for fellows with children.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single value - EMBO publishes country-dependent rates rather than one figure, ranging from EUR 51,600 to 99,600 per fellowship year in EMBC Member States and EUR 28,200 to 65,400 outside them
funding_period - the rate is expressed per fellowship year but is not published as a simple cadence such as per month

verification.notes: EMBO's own fellowship, benefits and guideline pages plus the official 2026 contract-rates PDF on embo.org were read in full. The country rate table, the EUR 2,500 childcare allowance, the exclusion of bench fees and overheads, the two-year duration, the hard 22 January 2027 cutoff and the one-candidate-per-host-lab and no-reapplication rule changes were all confirmed on the awarding body's domain.

applicant_utility.summary: Mobility is the hard filter, not publication count: EMBO will not fund you going back to the country where you did your PhD, to a lab you already worked in for more than six months, or to your PhD supervisor's lab, and the project cannot be a continuation of your doctorate. The money is country-dependent and paid either as an employment contract through your host institution or as a stipend, so a Swiss or Icelandic postdoc is worth roughly double a Bulgarian or Polish one. From Autumn 2027 you only get one shot - re-applications are banned - and from Autumn 2026 each host lab can back only one candidate per round, so agree with your prospective host before you file.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A recently graduated life-science PhD with a first-author paper who needs to change both country and research direction and wants a two-year funded postdoc abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the mobility rules first: different country from your PhD, and not your PhD lab, institute, department or supervisor.
Confirm your PhD date: if you already hold it, it must have been awarded within the two years before you submit.
Make sure the project is framed as a new direction, not an extension of your doctoral work.
Agree with your host lab that they will issue an employment contract if you are awarded, and confirm they are not supporting another candidate in the same round.
Have your first-author paper accepted or your preprint with public in-depth peer reviews ready - this is an eligibility criterion, not a nice-to-have.
Submit before the hard cutoff of 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET and plan to start within one calendar year of it.
common_rejection_risks: Applying to return to the country where the PhD was obtained.
Applying to a lab where you already spent more than six months, or to your former PhD supervisor.
A project that reviewers read as a direct continuation of the doctoral work.
Holding the PhD for more than two years at the time of application.
No first-author publication and no preprint with public in-depth peer reviews from an independent service.
Your host laboratory supporting a second candidate in the same round, which forces a withdrawal.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Bench fees, overheads, consumables and any other financial benefit to the host supervisor or receiving institute are explicitly not covered, so the host lab must find its own money for your experiments. Income from the stipend may also be taxable in certain countries, and fellows are responsible for national tax arrangements and their own social security where applicable.
document_audit: The application goes through the EMBO portal, but the host supervisor and host institution confirmation is a separate piece your prospective lab must stand behind.
Your first-author output must be verified as accepted or published - a preprint only counts if it has public in-depth peer reviews from an independent peer review service.
Hosts must agree that the EMBO grant is used to fund an employment contract, which requires their institutional sign-off, not just the supervisor's enthusiasm.
Child daycare and dependent child allowances apply only to non-EMBC fellows, so do not budget on them if your host is in an EMBC Member State.
alerts: From the Autumn 2027 round (applications after 22 January 2027 at 14:00 CET) re-applications will no longer be permitted - researchers may submit only one EMBO Fellowship Proposal.
From the Autumn 2026 selection round a host laboratory may support a maximum of one candidate per round, and excess applications will be withdrawn.
Part-time work at 50% or 75% is possible, but total full-time plus part-time duration may not exceed 36 months.
EMBO cannot advise on national tax regulations; contact the tax authorities in your host country.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You file one application for one project at one host laboratory through the EMBO portal before the round's hard cutoff, EMBO evaluates project excellence, track record and mobility, and on award EMBO transfers a country-rate grant to the host institution, which issues you an employment contract, or pays you a stipend in non-EMBC countries.
